3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: I couldn't tell if the sky was growing darker, or if it was just the tinted windows of the armored car.

4.speaker: Narrator
4.text: Our motorcade slowed as it approached the Zille border. A concrete barrier rose up in front of us, its top strung with barbed wire.

5.speaker: Narrator
5.text: My mother had insisted on accompanying me to the Wehzek-Rizian Friendship Day festivities. She leaned against the window, uncharacteristically quiet.

10.speaker: Estela Toras
10.text: "I'm thinking you ought to have chosen a different jacket to go with those trousers."

11.speaker: Estela Toras
11.text: "Say, might we have time for a quick detour once we reach town?"

12.speaker: Narrator
12.text: After a short while, she broke the silence.

14.speaker: Player_Romus
14.text: "No. I want to get this over with as fast as possible."

15.speaker: Estela Toras
15.text: "That's perfectly fine. Mind if I smoke?"

16.speaker: Narrator
16.text: She leaned forward and gave the driver an address. He nodded.

17.speaker: Narrator
17.text: Without waiting for an answer, she cracked open the window and lit a cigarette.

18.speaker: Narrator
18.text: At the border, we presented our identification documents and the official invitation from President Smolak. As we crossed, the road turned uneven.

19.speaker: Estela Toras
19.text: "Promise me you'll get these highways back up and running once Zille is returned."

21.speaker: Player_Romus
21.text: "It's at the top of my list."

23.speaker: Narrator
23.text: Factory smokestacks rose up on either side of us. Through the haze, I spotted numerous shanty towns, built over the past few years to house miners and refinery workers.

24.speaker: Narrator
24.text: We entered the city and drove on through a maze of tenement buildings, their facades hastily repainted to hide the damage from the war 20 years ago.

26.speaker: Narrator
26.text: As my mother had instructed him to, the driver veered down a side street that led toward the coast.

30.speaker: Narrator
30.text: We stopped in front of a small wooden building with a collapsed roof. The front porch was partly buried in sand; jagged teeth of broken glass lined the window frames.

31.speaker: Estela Toras
31.text: "They say you can't go home again. Rarely do they mean it this literally."

33.speaker: Player_Romus
33.text: "I can't believe this is the same place we used to go every summer."

37.speaker: Player_Romus
37.text: "Don't be so dramatic, Mother. It's just a house."

38.speaker: Player_Romus
38.text: "Wehlen will pay for what happened to your homeland."

42.speaker: Estela Toras
42.text: "I never brought my parents here after they fled to Rizia. I knew it would break their hearts."

43.speaker: Narrator
43.text: She put a hand on my shoulder.

44.speaker: Estela Toras
44.text: "I wish they could have seen it one last time. The way it used to be."

46.speaker: Narrator
46.text: I thought back to my carefree summers in Zille. My grandparents had spent the last 10 years of their lives in Palas Rezna, surrounded by luxury, but they never seemed as happy as they did in this house.

50.speaker: Narrator
50.text: I tried to summon memories of my grandparents. They'd spent the last 10 years of their lives in Palas Rezna, surrounded by luxury, yet they always seemed ill at ease.

51.speaker: Estela Toras
51.text: "Enough dallying. Driver, step on it. We've got a date with a psychopath."

52.speaker: Narrator
52.text: We returned to the main road and drove towards Smolak Square, a circular plaza in the center of town that had once been named after Duke Fedo Sazon.

53.speaker: Narrator
53.text: We both fell silent. After a few moments, she plastered a smile on her face.

54.speaker: Narrator
54.text: We kept going in the direction of Smolak Square, a circular plaza in the center of town that had once been named after Duke Fedo Sazon.

55.speaker: Player_Romus
55.text: "They could have stayed. Plenty of Rizians did."

56.speaker: Player_Romus
56.text: "You did everything you could for them. They should have been more grateful."

57.speaker: Player_Romus
57.text: "I'll have it fixed up one day. It'll be our summer home again."

58.speaker: Estela Toras
58.text: "No. Not after that horrible civil war. The only way they could have stayed is if I hadn't convinced Valero to get Wehlen involved in our affairs."

59.speaker: Narrator
59.text: A silver stretch limousine was parked just in front of the square. Our driver stopped and we exited the car, flanked by our guards.

60.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
60.text: "Your Majesty King Romus! Queen Mother Estela!"

61.speaker: Narrator
61.text: He made a sweeping, exaggerated bow and straightened up with a grin.

62.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
62.text: "Welcome to Wehlen. Please, make yourselves at home."

63.speaker: Player_Romus
63.text: "Actually, Mr. President, this *is* my home. I spent my childhood summers here."

65.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
65.text: "Who is this Mr. President? Call me Wiktor. We're friends, right?"

66.speaker: Player_Romus
66.text: "Mr. President. I wish I could say I was happy to be here."

67.speaker: Narrator
67.text: He gestured out to the square, where a colorful banner reading '24 Years Of Wehzek-Rizian Friendship' hung above a trio of gleaming tanks.

68.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
68.text: "Of course, of course. My home is your home, your home is my home. We're friends!"

69.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
69.text: "Why so glum, Your Majesty? How could anyone not be happy on a day like this?"

70.speaker: Estela Toras
70.text: "Say what you will about Smolak, he never makes a dull entrance."

71.speaker: Narrator
71.text: A dozen uniformed soldiers hurriedly got into formation around us and the limo. The door opened, and Wiktor Smolak stepped out.

72.speaker: Player_Romus
72.text: "Ah, yes. Nothing symbolizes friendship like heavy artillery."

73.speaker: Player_Romus
73.text: "Looks impressive. Where did you get those tanks?"

74.speaker: Player_Romus
74.text: "It's my first time at one of these ceremonies. What's going to happen?"

75.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
75.text: "Exactly! Who doesn't love tanks? Today's audience certainly does."

76.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
76.text: "The usual. I make a speech, you make a speech, the press takes pictures, everyone goes home happy. Listen to the crowd! They're already happy."

77.speaker: Player_Romus
77.text: "I've been wanting to speak with you about the terms of this *friendship.*"

78.speaker: Narrator
78.text: The square was surrounded by grandstands -- one side decorated in the colors of Wehlen's flag, the other in Rizia's blue, orange and gold. I heard loud cheers emanating from them.

79.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
79.text: "In due time, Your Majesty. First we have some speeches to get through. We can't let down our adoring public!"

80.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
80.text: "Rizia isn't Wehlen's only friend, Your Majesty."

81.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
81.text: "I've invited the finest representatives from both of our countries to join us for this special occasion. Follow me, if you will."

82.speaker: Estela Toras
82.text: "Grateful for what? If I hadn't convinced Valero to get Wehlen involved in our affairs, they never would have had to leave."

83.speaker: Estela Toras
83.text: "That ship has sailed, child. Just think, If I hadn't convinced Valero to get Wehlen involved in our affairs, none of this would've happened."

84.speaker: Narrator
84.text: She looked down at her hands.

85.speaker: Estela Toras
85.text: "The Wehzek president back then was such an upstanding man. How could I have known he'd go and get himself killed?"

86.speaker: Narrator
86.text: A semicircular stage was set up in front of the tanks. The crowd roared as we crossed the square and made our way over to it. Looking up into the grandstands, I noticed armed guards standing on every level.

87.speaker: Narrator
87.text: My mother and I took our seats. Wiktor stepped up to the microphone.

89.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
89.text: "Two dozen years ago, the glorious country of Wehlen was given custody over this land. A great honor, and a tremendous responsibility."

90.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
90.text: "Wehlen didn't only gain new territory that day. We gained new friends."

91.speaker: Narrator
91.text: He gestured meaningfully towards the Rizian side of the stands. After a few seconds, they broke out in scattered applause. My mother muttered a harsh-sounding curse in Zille dialect.

92.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
92.text: "Together, we have overcome war, repaired our economy and made great strides in science and industry."

93.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
93.text: "I look forward to strengthening that bond for many, many years to come!"

94.speaker: Narrator
94.text: He stepped to the side and pulled a rope attached to a flagpole. A massive Wehzek flag unfurled, then a much smaller Rizian one.

95.speaker: Estela Toras
95.text: "A captive audience. That would explain the enthusiasm."

96.speaker: Player_Romus
96.text: "Disgusting. This whole ceremony is a sham."

97.speaker: Player_Romus
97.text: "Nice idea. The crowd at my coronation sounded lackluster by comparison."

98.speaker: Player_Romus
98.text: "Maybe they're happy. They don't get many excuses for celebration around here."

99.speaker: Player_Romus
99.text: "Look at the sloppy way they're holding their guns. They have nothing on our recruits."

107.speaker: Player_Romus
107.text: "I stand before you at the dawning of a new era. The reign of Valero Toras is over."

108.speaker: Player_Romus
108.text: "You may not know it, but I am a grandson of Zille. The Queen Mother and I have deep ties to this land."

109.speaker: Player_Romus
109.text: "It is an honor to be here in Zille on the anniversary of our historic treaty."

110.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
110.text: "Today, I am especially delighted to be blessed with the presence of Rizia's new king. As well as the Queen Mother, of course."

111.speaker: Player_Romus
111.text: "Quiet. We're supposed to play nice, remember?"

112.speaker: Player_Romus
112.text: "I know. I can't believe this guy."

114.speaker: Estela Toras
114.text: "'May your testicles be stung by a thousand jellyfish.'"

115.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
115.text: "Even the decision of the Toras family to ally with Rumburg, a nation that obviously wishes Wehlen harm, could not diminish the beautiful bond we have formed."

116.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
116.text: "They are heirs to a long, proud legacy. One that would have been shattered had Wehlen and Rizia not made the fateful decision to work hand in hand."

118.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
118.text: "Please give a warm welcome to King Romus Toras!"

126.speaker: Narrator
126.text: "Glory to Rizia!" echoed the Rizian side of the stands. Wiktor gave me an appraising glance, then readjusted the microphone.

128.speaker: Narrator
128.text: Both sides of the stands applauded. Wiktor gave me an appraising glance, then readjusted the microphone.

129.speaker: Narrator
129.text: Loud applause broke out from the Wehzeks in the audience. Wiktor shot me an appraising glance, then turned back to his microphone.

130.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
130.text: "What a speech! The king's got charisma!"

131.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
131.text: "We have a terrific evening of entertainment lined up. But first, we must commemorate this landmark meeting of world leaders with a traditional triple-tank salute!"

132.speaker: Narrator
132.text: There was a rumbling from behind us as the three tanks aimed their barrels into the air. My mother and I looked at each other.

134.speaker: Narrator
134.text: The tank on the left fired, sending a plume of gold-colored smoke high over the stands. The crowd gasped in excitement.

135.speaker: Player_Romus
135.text: "That's the first time I've heard of this tradition."

139.speaker: Estela Toras
139.text: "We can thank his Eastern benefactors, I presume."

140.speaker: Narrator
140.text: Wiktor raised a finger up in the air.

142.speaker: Narrator
142.text: The gun mounted to the tank on the right went off. This time, the smoke was magenta.

144.speaker: Narrator
144.text: His count was interrupted by an unidentified voice in the distance, shouting "For the King!"

147.speaker: Narrator
147.text: Wiktor whipped his head around in shock, a frenzied look in his eyes. I turned to my mother.

148.speaker: Player_Romus
148.text: "If he was so upstanding, he wouldn't have agreed to stomp out a democratic revolution."

150.speaker: Estela Toras
150.text: "What revolution? If those terrorists were acting on behalf of the Rizian people, they wouldn't have harmed innocents. Yourself included."

151.speaker: Player_Romus
151.text: "It's not your fault. Father should have reneged on the agreement immediately after the assassination."

152.speaker: Player_Romus
152.text: "It was a period of instability across all of Merkopa. You were playing with fire."

153.speaker: Estela Toras
153.text: "And made outright enemies of Wehlen while our own country was still weak? Don't be foolish."

154.speaker: Estela Toras
154.text: "Would you have done any differently if Vina was in danger?"

156.speaker: Narrator
156.text: A deafening blast, much louder than the two that had preceded it, echoed from the opposite end of the square.

163.speaker: Player_Romus
163.text: "I had an interesting talk with Pabel recently."

164.speaker: Estela Toras
164.text: "Oh? I'm glad the two of you are still close."

168.speaker: Estela Toras
168.text: "He talks? I always saw him as a sort of walking hors d'oeuvre platter."

169.speaker: Player_Romus
169.text: "Was Father acting out of the ordinary the night of his death?"

170.speaker: Player_Romus
170.text: "When was the last time you saw Father? Before he died, I mean."

173.speaker: Estela Toras
173.text: "I told you, we had dinner together. After he made Pabel taste the food."

174.speaker: Estela Toras
174.text: "Any more out of the ordinary than ordinary, you mean?"

175.speaker: Estela Toras
175.text: "No. He went to bed early, as he'd been doing for months. A symptom of old age, for some."

176.speaker: Estela Toras
176.text: "I've never heard of her. Is she a noble?"

177.speaker: Player_Romus
177.text: "Tell me again. How did you discover Father had died?"

179.speaker: Estela Toras
179.text: "I told you. I went to check on him a few hours after supper."

184.speaker: Estela Toras
184.text: "And they say butlers have no imaginations."

185.speaker: Estela Toras
185.text: "Your father had a long list of enemies, and an equally long list of safeguards against them. His worries were what stopped his heart."

186.speaker: Estela Toras
186.text: "How cruel of you to pique my interest like that."

187.speaker: Narrator
187.text: She folded her arms and was silent for a while.

189.speaker: Player_Romus
189.text: "None of this was Wehlen's fault. It was the superpowers trying to use the country as a pawn."

190.speaker: Estela Toras
190.text: "Nobody forced Wiktor Smolak to turn my homeland into his country's armpit."

194.speaker: Player_Romus
194.text: "Actually, Mr. President, this *is* my mother's home."

195.speaker: Player_Romus
195.text: "It's heartening to see that Zille remains in good hands."

196.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
196.text: "Yes, yes! This square used to be gray and boring. Now look at it."

197.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
197.text: "It'll be your turn to speak in a minute, Your Majesty."

198.speaker: Player_Romus
198.text: "My mistake. Please go on, Mr. President."

199.speaker: Player_Romus
199.text: "Forgive me, but your words were so inspiring I couldn't stay quiet for a moment longer."

201.speaker: Narrator
201.text: Wiktor stared me down for a second. I suddenly became aware of how tall he was.

204.speaker: Narrator
204.text: Wiktor stared me down for a second. I suddenly became aware of how tall he was.

206.speaker: Narrator
206.text: He turned back to the crowd.

207.speaker: Narrator
207.text: I turned to face the crowd. The Rizian side of the stands erupted in loud, authentic-sounding applause.

210.speaker: Player_Romus
210.text: "It pained me when my father signed away this beautiful part of Rizia. Yet I knew it was for the greater good."

211.speaker: Player_Romus
211.text: "Today marks a chance to make a clean break with the past and begin looking towards the future."

212.speaker: Player_Romus
212.text: "I know none of the Rizians here today asked for their homeland to be governed by Wehlen. I myself had no choice in the matter."

213.speaker: Player_Romus
213.text: "I will never forget what Wehlen did for my family and my country."

214.speaker: Player_Romus
214.text: "I have come here to send Wiktor Smolak a warning. If Zille is not returned, he will face Rizia's full retaliation."

215.speaker: Player_Romus
215.text: "The past years have not been easy for any of you. But the time will soon come when we are reunited."

216.speaker: Player_Romus
216.text: "As ATO encroaches on our continent, it is vital that the nations of Southeastern Merkopa unite as one."

217.speaker: Player_Romus
217.text: "In one year, Rizia will resume governorship of Zille. But I hope that will not mean an end to our countries' friendly cooperation."

218.speaker: Player_Romus
218.text: "I commend Wiktor Smolak for his exemplary leadership in the face of war and terrorism."

219.speaker: Player_Romus
219.text: "To the Rizians here today, I say: Do not forget your motherland. Be ready to defend her if necessary."

220.speaker: Player_Romus
220.text: "I pledge to support Rizians and Wehzeks alike through the upcoming peaceful transfer of power."

221.speaker: Player_Romus
221.text: "I know that I can count on the President of Wehlen to do what's best for Zille until it is back in Rizia's custody."

222.speaker: Player_Romus
222.text: "Yet I commend Wiktor Smolak for his exemplary leadership in the face of war and terrorism."

225.speaker: Player_Romus
225.text: "I pledge to support Rizians and Wehzeks alike through the upcoming transfer of power."

226.speaker: Player_Romus
226.text: "I call on the people of Rizia to resist your Wehzek oppressors. Remind them in whose country they reside."

227.speaker: Player_Romus
227.text: "But I have come here to send Wiktor Smolak a warning. If Zille is not returned, he will face Rizia's full retaliation."

228.speaker: Narrator
228.text: The crowd went completely silent. Wiktor's mouth hung open in disbelief.

229.speaker: Player_Romus
229.text: "To my countrymen, I say: Be patient. A mere year from now, we will be reunited."

230.speaker: Player_Romus
230.text: "Despite our political differences, Rizia and Wehlen have much in common. There's no limit to what we can accomplish together."

231.speaker: Player_Romus
231.text: "Wiktor, I know you are a man of honor. When the time comes, you will do what is right."

232.speaker: Player_Romus
232.text: "The president of Wehlen believes these tanks will intimidate us. We will show him how wrong he is."

233.speaker: Player_Romus
233.text: "People of Wehlen, I invite you to stay in Zille once it is part of my kingdom again."

234.speaker: Player_Romus
234.text: "On behalf of House Toras, there will be justice for what has been done to Zille."

238.speaker: Narrator
238.text: A few tentative claps came from the Rizian side of the stands. I looked back at my mother. She spoke through gritted teeth.

240.speaker: Narrator
240.text: Wiktor's face remained placid. He readjusted his microphone, gripping it so tightly that his knuckles turned white.

241.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
241.text: "That was some speech, Your Majesty! And right in front of the international press, as well."

243.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
243.text: "Let's not allow King Romus to spoil the mood on this fine day. It's time to commemorate the occasion with a traditional three-tank salute!"

247.speaker: Narrator
247.text: Titus dove at me and tackled me to the ground. Screams of fear and confusion were rising up from all around.

248.speaker: Narrator
248.text: Titus rushed to cover me, gun at the ready. Screams of fear and confusion were rising up from all around.

252.speaker: Narrator
252.text: Titus rushed to our side, gun at the ready. Screams of fear and confusion were rising up from all around.

257.speaker: Narrator
257.text: My mother and Wiktor were still on the podium, surrounded by a thick cordon of Wehzek guards.

259.speaker: Player_Romus
259.text: "Don't you lay a hand on her, Smolak!"

260.speaker: Narrator
260.text: I turned towards the source of the sound and saw the Wehzek side of the stands engulfed in flames.

265.speaker: Narrator
265.text: Wiktor stood beside us on the podium, his own gun drawn. He was surrounded by a thick cordon of Wehzek guards.

266.speaker: Titus Gordion
266.text: "We've got to get you out of here."

267.speaker: Narrator
267.text: He and Smolak's guards exchanged a series of hand signals. The crowd had begun fleeing in every direction.

268.speaker: Titus Gordion
268.text: "They'll be fine. We have to get you out of here."

269.speaker: Narrator
269.text: He and Smolak's guards exchanged a series of hand signals. The crowd had begun fleeing in every direction.

270.speaker: Narrator
270.text: Titus grabbed my arm and swiftly started ushering me away. I took one last look back.

271.speaker: Narrator
271.text: Smoke was now rising from the Wehzek grandstand. Part of the structure had collapsed, and soldiers were working to free the people trapped underneath.

272.speaker: Narrator
272.text: The next few moments were a blur as we made our way through the panicked hordes of civilians. Wiktor's limo pulled up and Titus roughly shoved me inside.

274.speaker: Narrator
274.text: My mother's voice shook. She and Wiktor were sitting across from me, looking dazed.

275.speaker: Player_Romus
275.text: "We're going to get to the bottom of this."

278.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
278.text: "Of course she isn't. It seemed like *no Rizian* was harmed."

281.speaker: Narrator
281.text: Smolak had fire in his eyes.

282.speaker: Wiktor Smolak (R)
282.text: "If your people have anything to do with this, there will be a price to pay."

283.speaker: Narrator
283.text: He kept his eyes on me as the car began pulling away.
